executive_summary: Today's events reveal a dangerous overreliance on fragile infrastructure, whether digital, physical, or democratic. The vulnerability of our systems was underscored when technology stocks tumbled over escalating artificial intelligence spending concerns just as the MIT Technology Review detailed unprecedented cyberattacks on AI platforms. Simultaneously, a powerful earthquake in Japan exposed the physical fragility of urban centers through a catastrophic mall collapse with people feared trapped. This theme of systemic disruption extends directly into our political framework, where the Economist's newsletter highlights Donald Trump's appeal to the Supreme Court to restrict mail-in ballots. Ultimately, these converging crises demonstrate that our economic, structural, and electoral foundations face compounding threats that demand immediate fortification.

newsletters.title: The US in Brief: Mail-in ballots head to SCOTUS

items.headline: Mail-in ballots head to SCOTUS
items.blurb: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to allow it to implement an executive order, signed in March, that would tighten restrictions on mail-in ballots, after a federal appeals court this weekend upheld a ruling to block the order. The Supreme Court ruled against the administration in a separate voting case last month; the justices upheld a Mississippi law that allows the counting of postal ballots up to five days after an election if they are postmarked before the vote takes place.

items.headline: Michigan's Senate race final debate
items.blurb: Democratic candidates in Michigan’s Senate race held their final debate before a competitive primary next week that has transfixed the party . Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive former health official, criticised Haley Stevens, a moderate congresswoman, for her links to super PACs. He also vowed to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement. A win for Mr El-Sayed would be another boost to the left after victories in recent primaries in New York and Colorado.

items.headline: James Comey indictment
items.blurb: James Comey, a former head of the FBI, asked a judge to dismiss an indictment against him that claims he threatened to kill Donald Trump. Mr Comey is accused of sharing a cryptic social-media message calling for the president’s death; he denies inciting violence. The Justice Department has brought other charges against Mr Comey since Mr Trump returned to the presidency. In November a judge dismissed a separate case in which the administration accused him of obstructing Congress and making a false statement to lawmakers.

items.headline: Prediction markets ban suspended in Minnesota
items.blurb: A federal judge in Minnesota suspended a ban on prediction markets, arguing that it may be overruled by federal law. The Trump administration had sued the state after it enacted legislation to ban markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket from August 1st. Both outfits welcomed the judge’s ruling. States including California and New Jersey are mulling whether to introduce similar restrictions.

items.headline: Funeral of Lindsey Graham
items.blurb: World leaders and other dignitaries will be in Washington today for the funeral of Lindsey Graham, a senator from South Carolina who died on July 11th . Mr Graham was a foreign-policy hawk who relished his role as an informal envoy for Mr Trump. The president is expected to meet Binyamin Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister, and Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukraine’s president, both of whom are attending.
